highlights.title: Stack previews on the desktop Sky map
highlights.body: Completed mono and colour stacks now appear in Sky when Stacks when zoomed is on and you zoom past 3×. Existing stacks work without rebuilding them.

highlights.title: Windows desktop startup
highlights.body: The app finishes starting instead of remaining on Checking access. Its local server keeps one socket across restarts.

highlights.title: Frames copied between image folders
highlights.body: Previews work while the same frame is in two image folders. PSF Guard reads the largest copy with matching capture headers and still refuses files of different captures.

highlights.title: Frames off the planned rotation
highlights.body: Quality analysis flags fresh solves more than 5° from the target's planned rotation and leaves those frames out of stack previews. Meridian flips still match. If the plan changed after capture, set the target's rotation to the angle you want.

highlights.title: Safer HTTPS connections
highlights.body: PSF Guard no longer trusts HTTPS certificates issued through emSign intermediate certificates that browsers have stopped trusting. This covers update checks, sync and catalog downloads.

deprecations.title: PSF Guard is moving to its own catalogs
deprecations.body:
For new Target Scheduler databases, choose Settings → Databases → Import from Target Scheduler to import the database and set up sync.

Your current Target Scheduler setup will keep working in 0.12. A later update will create a PSF Guard catalog for you and keep captures, plans and grades in sync with Target Scheduler.

Separate catalogs let us add features to PSF Guard and support new Target Scheduler versions. We plan to remove direct database access in 0.13 or later.

upgradeNotes.title: Choose how Target Scheduler syncs
upgradeNotes.body: New Target Scheduler connections create a PSF Guard-owned catalog. Local-file imports enable automatic sync and grade writeback; review the startup, change detection and schedule settings after importing. Grade writeback has its own switch. Manual planning and grade transfers use Preview and Apply. Director activation sends approved planning through the saved TS connection and retries failed deliveries.

upgradeNotes.title: Allow time for calibration checks and rebuilds
upgradeNotes.body: The first start reads frame sites, grades calibration frames and measures flat groups in the background. Stacks and masters rebuild once when you next use them. PSF Guard does not reuse plate solves or satellite predictions made by 0.11, so it solves frames again. Work you start takes priority over these checks.

upgradeNotes.title: Review new targets and planning changes
upgradeNotes.body: Automatic image-folder import now holds frames for unknown targets for Review. Change New targets in the database settings to create projects automatically. Before activating a plan, check its preview: activation turns off exposure plans the plan does not include. Take Target Scheduler’s values keeps plans made in N.I.N.A.

upgradeNotes.title: Keep a copy of settings before a downgrade
upgradeNotes.body: PSF Guard 0.11 can open catalogs graded by 0.12, but it ignores the new calibration grades and choices apart from darks graded for stray light. Saving settings in an older version drops the new calibration settings and rig overrides.

highlights.title: Keep your catalog separate from Target Scheduler
highlights.body: Import a Target Scheduler database into a PSF Guard catalog, or pair the PSF Guard Sync plugin. Keep captures, plans and grades in sync, with grade conflicts reported for review.

highlights.title: Inspect calibration frames and masters
highlights.body: Review calibration grades, compare frames with their sessions, trace master inputs and repair duplicate records. Keep a frame out or use it anyway without deleting its file.

highlights.title: Match flats by their measured pattern
highlights.body: Group flats across nights by measured light patterns and dust changes. Inspect dust and vignetting, split or join groups, and choose which side of a change supplies a light’s flats.

highlights.title: Stretch stacks and combine color
highlights.body: Use Median anchor or Layered alongside the default Auto MTF stretch. Install Gaia colors to calibrate RGB, LRGB and one-shot-color stacks. Combine WBPP masters in their own color card. Rebuilt stacks keep your processing choices.

highlights.title: Plan mosaics across rigs
highlights.body: Place and rotate panels separately, preserve panels already captured and preview what each rig will shoot. Resend an activation to a site that missed it. In the Starfront collaboration beta, deliver accepted lights with calibration frames or completed stacks.

highlights.title: Back up now or on a schedule
highlights.body: Save settings, accounts, plans and catalogs in one archive. Download it, save it to a folder, or schedule daily or weekly backups with retention limits.

highlights.title: Review images on any screen
highlights.body: Browse by each rig’s observing night, select Sequence frames by score, stars or HFR, and keep charts in view. Compact phone layouts leave more room for images. Desktop Zoom in and Zoom out resize the whole UI.

highlights.title: Control background work
highlights.body: Follow progress and reorder queued builds in the header’s jobs list. Pause automatic quality analysis, preview pre-generation, flat measuring or frame-site reading until Resume or a server restart. Builds and color requests survive restarts, and work you start takes priority.

upgradeNotes.title: Docker settings moved
upgradeNotes.body: Settings now live in /data/config/psf-guard and the cache in /data/cache. If you mounted /home/psfguard/.config, copy its psf-guard folder into /data/config/ before starting 0.11, or your databases and users will be missing.

upgradeNotes.title: Allow time for the first start
upgradeNotes.body: PSF Guard backs up each catalog and updates its calibration tables. A background pass then measures raw darks. Stacks, masters and colour composites rebuild once when you next use them.

upgradeNotes.title: Cache cleanup starts at 90% disk use
upgradeNotes.body: PSF Guard removes previews, checkpoints and unused masters it can rebuild. It never removes stacks. Change the limit in Settings › Storage. Read the full release notes before going back to 0.10.5.

highlights.title: Plan across rigs
highlights.body: Frame targets, set goals per filter and share the work between rigs. Preview each plan before writing it to Target Scheduler.

highlights.title: Build and review stacks in one place
highlights.body: Stacks has its own view, with noise-weighted builds, colour previews and WBPP runs.

highlights.title: Check calibration before stacking
highlights.body: Find lights your library cannot calibrate and keep darks with stray light out of masters.

highlights.title: Connect an agent
highlights.body: Let an MCP agent work with catalogs, plans and stacks within your account's access limits.
